techniques.name: Wordmark soft reveal from the right
techniques.description: The italic serif wordmark appears centred, last letter first: a soft-edged mask travels right to left while opacity ramps, 14 frames at the open over a photo plate (F1–F15), 11 frames at the close on white (F1149–F1159). Same move bookends the film, so the close reads as a return.
techniques.routeReason: A masked, eased reveal on a vector mark; MaskedLine with a horizontal gradient mask set per frame reproduces it, no 3D or shader needed.

techniques.name: Rising sheet wipe with long tail
techniques.description: A flat sheet of the next ground (dark green, later off-white) rises from the bottom over a still plate. Fast first third (6% → 55% of height between F52 and F56), then a long tail; a sliver of the old plate stays at the top until F74 (green) or F488 (off-white). The next scene's first element (a stroke ring, then interface panels) starts drawing on the sheet before it is finished.
techniques.routeReason: A clip-path inset animated per frame over two layers; the existing transitions do not include a bottom-up cover with an eased front and an unfinished tail, so it is a short custom presentation.

techniques.name: Word-by-word line that stays centred
techniques.description: A single light-weight sans line is built one word at a time. Each word fades in and rises a few pixels over about 5 frames; the line as a whole slides so that the growing sentence stays near frame centre (OCR line centre 0.40 → 0.50 → 0.41 → 0.51 of width as words arrive). Gaps: 9 frames, 28 frames, 13 frames on the thesis line; 2, 5, 5, 6 frames on the promise line; 9 frames between number and noun on the stat.
techniques.routeReason: Per-word timing driven from a cue list; HeadlineBuild or SplitText can stagger words, and the re-centring is a measured line width interpolated per frame.

ease.name: power2.out
evidence: visuals/a1/s02-wipe-tail.jpg F74–F79 word settles upward in about 5 frames

typography.entry: word by word, fade + 4–6 px rise over 5 frames, line re-centres

techniques.name: Whole frame shrinks into the product object
techniques.description: The full-frame titled shot gains a thin off-white border and shrinks, keeping its 16:9 proportion, to a slab about 40% of frame width on a warm off-white ground; a diagonal sheen crosses it; its text fades as it shrinks. Then the slab narrows to button proportions and an icon spins in.
techniques.routeReason: A layout morph between a full-frame scene and a rounded rectangle; GrowToScene run in reverse, or LayoutMorph, holds the scene inside the morphing rectangle.

ease.name: power2.inOut
evidence: visuals/a1/s02-shrink-to-card.jpg DIFF rises 0.59 → 25.62 (F171) then falls to 2.04 (F182)

techniques.name: Action button types its label, then flips open as the product
techniques.description: The button's label types in one letter per about 2 frames (F189–F212) behind a spinning plus icon; the button then holds about 1 s, rotates on its horizontal axis to edge-on (F241–F245), and opens from the other side as the full product object in perspective (F246–F251), settling by F260.
techniques.routeReason: The typing is TypedLine; the flip is a per-frame rotateX on two faces with backface hidden, then back to a 2D transform once settled (the motion AGENTS trap on 3D transforms). The object's metal face is a rendered still from the Blender stage (t06).

techniques.name: Rendered product object fanned and orbited
techniques.description: Photoreal brushed-metal objects (green and silver variants) close to camera, slowly rotating; the green one fans into a stack of a dozen copies that spread like a deck (F327–F380). Strong specular sweeps across the surface; shallow depth of field. Motion energy peaks around 10–12 s from the object, not from editing.
techniques.routeReason: Believable metal, specular sweeps and soft shadow are the point of the shot (blender-3d: for a shot the viewer should take for a photograph). Played back through the blender-plate block. A three.js fan is the cheaper fallback if the material may look graphic.

techniques.name: Soft organic matte to an atmospheric plate
techniques.description: A cloud-shaped, soft-edged matte opens from the right over the moving object shot, revealing a storm-cloud plate in 11 frames (F403–F413); the edge carries a slight chromatic fringe; the first word of the next line appears at F407, inside the revealed area.
techniques.routeReason: An organic luma-matte transition is a shader look whose shape matters more than its parameters; a Hyperframes shader transition (domain warp or noise dissolve) fits. In Remotion the nearest equivalent is a large blurred radial mask animated across the frame.

evidence: audio.json beat 13.398 within 0.035 s of the start

sound.note: Start sits 0.035 s from a beat and an onset (measured); whether a hit or whoosh is there is not known. Not heard.

techniques.name: Interface panels grow from a sliver, staggered
techniques.description: Inside the rising off-white sheet, the first panel appears as a 1-pixel vertical line (F458), opens to a portrait card (F465) and then to a landscape card (F472); the panels below follow 3–4 frames apart; then each panel's illustration and text fade in (F469–F506).
techniques.routeReason: The panels are the real product interface (real-UI rule: capture the actual page with capture:app); the growth is a per-panel clip or scale animation on the capture's regions, which DashboardAssemble already stages.

techniques.name: Flash montage under one continuous caption
techniques.description: Five destination plates cut every 4 frames (one of 3), then a sixth held 37 frames. One caption at a fixed position (y ≈ 0.45 of height, starting x ≈ 0.19 of width): only the place name changes per plate, and the trailing words keep revealing across the cuts so the sentence completes on the last flash.
techniques.routeReason: Real places from the air: stock aerials with licence evidence (engine-selection: places are footage). The caption over them is Remotion.

techniques.name: Stat line over a pulling-out line-particle sphere
techniques.description: Hard cut to the dark brand green; a sphere drawn from short curved green strokes pulls out (z −0.62) and turns; the number fades in at +5 frames, the noun at +14 frames, line re-centring as it grows; held 2.5 s.
techniques.routeReason: Seeded strokes on a sphere projected per frame (three.js through @remotion/three or 2D projection); a flat green ground and light type keep it browser-cheap.

techniques.name: Edge-in light bloom to off-white while a device rises
techniques.description: The dark green frame brightens from the edges inward like an overexposed vignette (centre stays green longest) to an off-white ground in 10 frames (F842–F851), while a phone rises from the bottom edge; the headline then slides down into the top of frame.
techniques.routeReason: A radial-gradient mask whose inner radius closes per frame over the outgoing scene, plus a translate on the device layer; the device screen itself is a third-party wallet sheet and must be a pixel-faithful replica from a dated screenshot (real-UI rule).

techniques.name: Anthem run: fixed lead phrase, italic value word per plate
techniques.description: Six plates, 29–36 frames each, hard cuts. Centred one-line slogan: upright light sans lead (on screen at the cut) plus an italic serif value word that fades up over about 8 frames. The lead changes once (negation, then affirmation); the last plate is pure white with the value word in brand green, held 49 frames, faded out over 10 frames.
techniques.routeReason: Five evocative stock plates (fence, clock, traffic trails, golden hour, skyline) carry the meanings; the type is Remotion. The white final plate is pure Remotion.

evidence: recomputed: 5 of 7 anthem cuts within 80 ms of a beat vs 0.29 chance, n = 7
